title: Style/content image pair (Starry Night style, Valensole lavender-field content)
content:
All NST notebooks use one style image, Van Gogh's "Starry Night" (Wikimedia Google Art Project JPG),
and one content image, a lavender-field sunset near Valensole (.avif). Both were uploaded to the Colab
/content directory and are not in the repo. Images are resized and center-cropped to 384 px (512 px in
notebook 01) and ImageNet-normalised. Note: notebook 01's wget fallback produced a 0-byte style.jpg, so
the notebook read the uploaded /content copy. Notebook 02's fallback content URL is an unrelated PNG
transparency demo, so the result depends on the upload being present.

extraction.evidence: 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cells 3-4 (image copy/wget, IMG_SIZE=384); 01_gaussianity_test (1).ipynb cell 2 output 'style.jpg size: 0 bytes', cell 4 loads /content/Van_Gogh... at size 512

title: VGG19 feature extractor at the five Gatys style layers
content:
torchvision VGG19 (IMAGENET1K_V1 weights, frozen, eval mode) truncated after relu5_1, returning
activations at relu1_1, relu2_1, relu3_1, relu4_1 and relu5_1 (feature indices 1, 6, 11, 20, 29), the
layers Gatys uses for the style loss. The same class is copied into all three notebooks. Content loss
uses relu4_1.

extraction.evidence: 01_gaussianity_test (1).ipynb cells 3-4 (VGGFeatures, layer_ids); identical class in 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cell 4

title: Three style losses - Gram (Gatys), AdaIN mean+std, sliced Wasserstein (random projections)
content:
Gatys loss: MSE between Gram matrices normalised by C*H*W, summed over the five layers. AdaIN loss: MSE
of per-channel means plus MSE of per-channel stds. Sliced Wasserstein (Heitz et al. 2021): project the
HW x C feature cloud onto n_proj random unit directions, sort, and take the MSE (1-D W2 squared per
projection). A fresh set of random directions is drawn on every call. The stylize() loop starts from
the content image and optimises pixels on style_w * style + content_w * content (relu4_1).

extraction.evidence: 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cell 6 (gram, gatys_loss, adain_loss, first sliced_wasserstein_loss) and cell 9 (stylize with LBFGS)

title: Sliced Wasserstein loss redefined with fixed seeded projections (for L-BFGS)
content:
Every notebook that runs SW redefines sliced_wasserstein_loss straight after the original. The new version
draws its projection directions from a generator seeded 42 + layer index, so they are the same on every
call, "for L-BFGS line search to work". It also adds 1e-8 to the norm and prints NaN/inf. The SW
objective is therefore a fixed set of n_proj 1-D marginals, not a stochastic estimate of the full sliced
distance: 16 directions in the notebook 02 runs, 64 in notebook 03. All SW-optimised outputs, and the
notebook 03 SW yardstick when evaluated after this cell, use this version.

extraction.evidence: 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cell 7 (gen_rng.manual_seed(42 + i)); same redefinition in 02_style_bakeoff (1).ipynb cell 6 and 03_distribution_analysis_(1).ipynb cell 7

title: Gram/AdaIN moment matching is only justified if VGG features are Gaussian
content:
Gatys, AdaIN and WCT match only the first and second moments of VGG activations. That matches the whole
distribution only if the per-channel distributions are Gaussian. Post-ReLU activations are non-negative
and sparse, so the assumption is suspect a priori. If features are not Gaussian, a loss that matches the
full distribution (sliced Wasserstein) should give visibly and measurably different stylisations from Gram
and AdaIN.
hypothesis: VGG post-ReLU features are not Gaussian, so first+second-moment style losses discard distributional information that a full-distribution loss (sliced Wasserstein) recovers.

extraction.evidence: 01_gaussianity_test (1).ipynb cell 0 (motivation) and cell 9; 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cell 1 ('If VGG features were Gaussian, all three should produce visually similar outputs')

title: Gaussianity test of VGG19 features on Starry Night: 0% of channels Gaussian at every layer
content:
Per-channel statistics of VGG19 activations on the 512 px style image, 5,000 sampled positions per
channel, D'Agostino K^2 test at p > 0.05. The fraction of exact zeros is 0.37, 0.62, 0.68, 0.81 and 0.78
from relu1_1 to relu5_1. Mean |skew| is 2.06 to 4.99 and excess kurtosis 10.87 to 39.51. No channel at any
layer passes the normality test (0.0%). relu2_1 skew and kurtosis are NaN, probably from constant
(all-zero) channels; this was not investigated. Single image, single seed.
hypothesis: VGG post-ReLU features are not Gaussian.

extraction.evidence: 01_gaussianity_test (1).ipynb cell 6 output table (layer / mean_zeros / |skew| / kurt / %chan Gaussian)

title: Style bake-off with L-BFGS - Gatys vs AdaIN vs SW (16 fixed projections)
content:
Same content, style and optimiser for three losses: L-BFGS with strong-Wolfe line search, lr 1.0, max_iter
250, pixels initialised from the content image, 384 px. Style weights are Gatys 1e6, AdaIN 1e2 and SW 1e3
(n_proj=16, fixed seeded projections). Losses at step 240: Gatys style 1.855e-06 / content 4.173;
AdaIN style 5.493e-03 / content 6.646; SW style 1.259e-02 / content 6.256. The comparison is visual only
(style_bakeoff.png, not committed). The notebook records no verdict.
hypothesis: If VGG features were Gaussian, all three losses should produce visually similar outputs.

extraction.evidence: 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cell 9 (stylize, LBFGS), cells 10-11 outputs (step 240 losses), cell 13 (reading guide, no verdict)

title: Style bake-off rerun with AdamW (lr 0.1, 240 steps) instead of L-BFGS
content:
A day-later copy of the bake-off that swaps L-BFGS for AdamW (lr 0.1, eps 1e-8, 240 single steps).
Weights and the 16 fixed SW projections are unchanged. At step 240 every method ends with higher content
loss than under L-BFGS: Gatys 4.380 vs 4.173, AdaIN 7.781 vs 6.646, SW 7.955 vs 6.256. AdaIN and SW also
end with higher style loss (AdaIN 2.181e-02 vs 5.493e-03, SW 1.994e-02 vs 1.259e-02). The notebook gives no
reason for the switch, and the markdown still says L-BFGS.
hypothesis: If VGG features were Gaussian, all three losses should produce visually similar outputs.

extraction.evidence: 02_style_bakeoff (1).ipynb cell 8 (AdamW stylize, LBFGS commented out), cells 9-10 outputs (step 240 losses); compare 02_style_bakeoff.ipynb cells 10-11

title: Cross-metric table: AdaIN output, not SW output, is closest to the style under sliced Wasserstein
content:
Each stylised output (L-BFGS, 250 iters, SW trained with 64 fixed projections) is scored against the
style features with three yardsticks: Gram MSE, AdaIN MSE and SW distance (n_proj=256). SW distance:
content baseline 6.27, Gatys 0.547, SW output 0.422, AdaIN output 0.147. Gatys is worse than SW on the
full-distribution yardstick, as predicted. But the AdaIN output beats the SW-optimised output on SW's own
metric by about 3x. So "SW's own SW distance is much lower" does not hold here. One plausible cause is that
the SW loss matched only 64 fixed directions. The notebook does not discuss this.
hypothesis: A full-distribution loss (SW) leaves less distributional mismatch than Gram or AdaIN; the Gatys-row/SW-column gap measures the information Gatys ignores.

extraction.evidence: 03_distribution_analysis_(1).ipynb cell 5 output table (method / Gram MSE / AdaIN MSE / SW dist), cell 9 (SW trained n_proj=64), cell 10 (what to look for)

title: Per-layer SW distance - AdaIN output lowest at every VGG layer
content:
The same three outputs, scored by sliced Wasserstein squared per layer (256 fresh random projections). The
AdaIN output is lowest at all five layers (relu1_1 3.585e-03 ... relu4_1 7.984e-02). The SW output is worse
than Gatys at relu1_1 (7.301e-03 vs 4.965e-03), relu3_1 (6.502e-02 vs 4.013e-02) and relu5_1 (9.786e-02 vs
8.264e-02), and better only at relu2_1 and relu4_1 (2.192e-01 vs 3.924e-01). Every method is far below the
content baseline (relu4_1 2.239).
hypothesis: The per-layer breakdown shows which layers the second-order approximation breaks down hardest.

title: Write-up claim: moment matching is the wrong frame; distribution matching (SW) is the fix
content:
The notebook 03 write-up draws three claims. (1) The Gaussian assumption behind Gram/AdaIN is false at
every VGG layer (notebook 01, solid). (2) SW gives visibly different outputs, so non-Gaussianity matters
(notebook 02, visual only). (3) The Gatys-row/SW-column gap quantifies the discarded information. It
rejects explicit higher-order moment tensors (O(C^3)) in favour of implicit distribution matching (SW,
SANet/StyTR2), citing Heitz et al. CVPR 2021 and Kolkin et al. STROTSS. Claim (3) is undercut by the
repo's own numbers: AdaIN's output beats the SW output on the SW yardstick, both overall and at every layer.
hypothesis: The moment-matching frame was the wrong frame; distribution-matching is.

extraction.evidence: 03_distribution_analysis_(1).ipynb cell 16 ('The write-up section'); contradicting numbers in cell 5 and cell 14 outputs
